text: Wind farms might get more useful information from a smaller experiment. Researchers led by MIT used a pressurized wind tunnel to make model turbines behave more like full-scale machines in the atmosphere. That let them test how the rotor's alignment, blade angle, and tip speed affect power. They also checked a simpler computer model that engineers could use to explore turbine designs and control strategies. For viewers, the value is straightforward: better tests can help operators decide how to get more from existing equipment. The team estimates possible economic gains, but those are projections rather than field results, so the real-world improvement remains to be proven. A wind tunnel cannot reproduce every changing condition across a working farm, where neighbouring turbines affect one another and gusts shift across the site. It can, however, make a difficult engineering question easier to test. Now it needs field testing.
